markers.s: Log in to view the full text

paywall_academic.dist: vs botwall: status is 200 and the page carries real article metadata plus a subscribe/sign-in offer; a botwall would be 403/202 with under 60 visible-text chars and no article title.
paywall_academic.notes: Atypon platform. HTTP 200 with full navigation chrome; the article body itself is replaced by a login offer. body_text_chars stays high (~32k) because of nav/footer boilerplate, so text length alone is NOT a paywall signal here.

paywall_academic.dist: vs paywall_saas: the purchase language names a single article and an institution, not a seat or plan upgrade.
paywall_academic.notes: Also Atypon. 'Restricted access' plus a per-article purchase widget is the strongest academic-paywall pair observed.

paywall_academic.dist: vs nature_openaccess_NEGATIVE (same site, same template, HTTP 200): the ONLY reliable difference is the JSON-LD isAccessibleForFree value. Nothing in the visible chrome differs.
paywall_academic.notes: Best-case machine-readable paywall declaration: schema.org hasPart/cssSelector marks exactly which DOM subtree is gated. Redirect chain 303-302-302-200 through idp.nature.com is an IdP session bounce, NOT a login wall.

paywall_academic.dist: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Identical template and identical 303/302/302/200 redirect chain to nature_subscription; only isAccessibleForFree flips.
paywall_academic.notes: Include in the test corpus as a must-not-fire case. Proves that redirect chains through an identity provider, cookie-error query params, and Nature chrome are all paywall-neutral.

paywall_news.dist: vs login_required: FT returns 200 at the ORIGINAL article URL with the article title replaced by 'Subscribe to read'; a login wall redirects to a distinct /login URL.
paywall_news.notes: Full-body replacement paywall (Zephr). The response headers are decisive: x-host names a barrier-page origin and Set-Cookie carries an explicit DENIED access decision. Header evidence beats body evidence here.

paywall_news.dist: vs gdpr_consent: THE SAME FILE is also the gdpr_consent sample. Consent and paywall co-occur on EU publishers; a classifier must be able to emit both, or it will mislabel one as the other.
paywall_news.notes: Teaser paywall: real headline and lede are present, the rest is truncated. NOTE THE PARSING TRAP - isAccessibleForFree is the STRING "False", not the boolean false. A naive JSON-LD check for a false boolean misses it. Same fetch as gdpr_consent/lemonde_article.html; file copied, not re-requested.

paywall_news.distinguishing_from: Attempted as paywall_news, actually served a DataDome captcha. Filed under captcha/datadome_captcha_nytimes.html.
paywall_news.notes: NYT, WSJ (robots-disallowed anyway), Economist and Washington Post all refuse plain curl before any paywall logic runs. WaPo reset the TCP connection outright (curl error 56). To collect a real NYT/WaPo paywall body you need a real browser engine; the bot layer fires first.

paywall_saas.dist: vs paywall_news: no subscribe-to-read barrier and no article truncation; instead individual DATA VALUES inside otherwise-complete prose are swapped for button elements carrying data-paywall-trigger. Redaction-in-place, not replacement.
paywall_saas.notes: MOST IMPORTANT AMBIGUITY IN THE CORPUS: JSON-LD says isAccessibleForFree true while the page is demonstrably partially gated. Publisher-declared access metadata is a hint, never a verdict.

paywall_saas.dist: NEGATIVE CONTROL. The literal token paywall appears in this FREE story's bundled JS, and 'Sign in' appears in the nav. Substring matching on either would produce a false positive.
paywall_saas.notes: Medium exposes isLockedPreviewOnly; here it is false and the full story is served. Use this to punish keyword-only classifiers.

paywall_saas.distinguishing_from: Both intended as SaaS upgrade-gates; both returned bot challenges instead (Cloudflare 403 and AWS WAF 202). Filed under botwall/.
paywall_saas.notes: paywall_saas is the thinnest category here: the SaaS products with the clearest upgrade gates are also the ones most aggressively bot-protected, so a plain HTTP client sees the botwall, never the paywall. Collect this class from authenticated production traffic instead.

login_required.dist: CANONICAL login wall: the request URL and the final URL differ, and the final URL contains a return parameter pointing back at the original. That redirect-with-return-param shape is the single most reliable login signal in this corpus.
login_required.notes: HTTP 200 at the END of the chain. Status code is useless; the redirect chain is everything.

markers.s: <title>Login or Sign Up for a Dropbox Account</title>

login_required.dist: Same shape as github_settings (302 to /login with a continuation param). body_text_chars is 38, near zero, because the login UI is client-rendered, so an emptiness heuristic would confuse this with a broken page.
login_required.notes: Best example of a login wall whose HTML carries almost no text. Classify from the Location header and the title, not the body.

login_required.dist: vs http_404: a nonexistent DOI was requested, and instead of 404 the site redirected twice to a SESSION-COOKIE interstitial and returned 200. Neither the requested resource's absence nor a login requirement is stated anywhere.
login_required.notes: IMPORTANT EDGE CASE. The same host returned a normal 200 article for a valid DOI in this same run, so /action/cookieAbsent is not a blanket wall. Demonstrates that one host can serve several wall types depending on path validity and cookie state.

login_required.dist: WEAK SAMPLE, kept deliberately. This is a browser-capability interstitial that also offers sign-in, not a true auth redirect. A classifier keying on 'Sign in' alone will call this login_required; keying on a redirect-with-return-param will correctly not.
login_required.notes: HTTP 200, no redirect, 912 visible-text chars. Use as a hard case rather than a clean positive.

markers.s: Pandora is unavailable in this country or region

geo_blocked.dist: vs login_required: also a 302-then-200 redirect, but the destination path is /restricted and the copy names a COUNTRY OR REGION rather than an account. Region language is the separator, not the redirect.
geo_blocked.notes: Only genuine geo-block body collected. Egress IP was South Korea. Explicit HTTP 302 to a dedicated restricted page.

geo_blocked.dist: NEGATIVE CONTROL. BBC iPlayer is UK-only, yet from a Korean IP it served the complete 823KB homepage with HTTP 200 and no region notice anywhere in the HTML.
geo_blocked.notes: Geo enforcement happens at the playback/API layer, not the landing document. Proves geo_blocked is largely UNDETECTABLE from landing-page HTML.

geo_blocked.dist: NEGATIVE CONTROL. UK-only service, HTTP 200, 44 visible-text chars (empty SPA shell). Near-zero text would trip an emptiness heuristic even though nothing is blocked at this layer.
geo_blocked.notes: Akamai-served (X-Akamai-Transformed header, _abck cookie) but NOT challenged.

geo_blocked.dist: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Norway-only catalogue, HTTP 200, full Norwegian chrome, no geo notice.
geo_blocked.notes: Third independent confirmation that broadcaster geo-blocks are invisible in the landing HTML.

geo_blocked.distinguishing_from: Not an HTML wall at all: the connection simply never returned data.
geo_blocked.notes: curl error 28, timed out after 25s with 0 bytes received, on robots.txt. A network-level geo-drop produces NO document to classify. Detectable only from timing plus zero bytes, never from HTML.

markers.s: YOU MUST BE OF LEGAL DRINKING AGE TO ENTER THIS SITE.

age_gated.dist: vs gdpr_consent: both are full-page interstitials with an accept action, but the age gate asks about the VISITOR'S AGE or birth date and offers a country selector, while a consent wall asks about data processing and carries __tcfapi or a named CMP vendor script.
age_gated.notes: Cleanest age gate collected: the requirement is stated in plain server-rendered text, not just in class names.

age_gated.dist: vs http_404: HTTP 200 and the title is the real product title (Save 75% on Red Dead Redemption 2 on Steam), so a title-based heuristic sees a normal product page. The gate lives in the URL path and the form ids.
age_gated.notes: Content-maturity gate rather than a legal-purchase gate. The path segment /agecheck/ is itself the strongest signal.

age_gated.dist: HARD CASE: the full marketing homepage is served (5779 visible-text chars) and the gate is applied client-side. Markup for the gate is present, but the page does not LOOK gated to a text-only reader.
age_gated.notes: Markers appear once each inside component config, not in rendered copy. Shows why age_gated needs markup and class-name matching, not visible-text matching.

markers.s: Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker

captcha.dist: vs botwall/datadome_block_economist.html: essentially the same template and the same 403. The only differences are the DataDome response-type field ('rt':'c' here vs 'rt':'i' there) and the script it loads (c.js vs i.js). c means interactive captcha, i means hard block. Nothing else separates a solvable captcha from a refusal.
captcha.notes: THE most valuable discrimination in this corpus and the least obvious. Also note x-datadome-riskscore: 0.874769287384864, the vendor telling you why it fired.

captcha.distinguishing_from: Classic reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha interstitials could not be triggered honestly.
captcha.notes: Google's /sorry/index captcha is unreachable without abusive query volume and /search is robots-disallowed for *. hCaptcha and Turnstile interstitials appear only after a challenge escalates. Collect opportunistically from production traffic by matching www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js, hcaptcha.com/1/api.js, or challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile in a live response.

botwall.dist: vs paywall_academic: this WAS an academic article request. The response never reached the publisher's paywall logic. Cf-Mitigated: challenge is the decisive header; Server: cloudflare alone appears on science.org and journals.sagepub.com too, which both returned normal articles.
botwall.notes: Cloudflare Managed Challenge, 403. Body is 5.9KB decompressed (3.3KB on the wire) of inline CSS and a Turnstile mount point.

botwall.dist: vs tandfonline_cf_challenge: SAME vendor, SAME Cf-Mitigated header, DIFFERENT title string (One moment please vs Just a moment). Title-string matching alone will miss one of the two.
botwall.notes: Kept specifically to break brittle title-only Cloudflare detectors.

markers.s: Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker

botwall.dist: vs captcha/datadome_captcha_nytimes.html: same template, but 'rt':'i' and i.js mean hard block rather than solvable captcha.
botwall.notes: Set-Cookie includes user_geo_country=KR, so the site correctly geolocated the request yet blocked on bot score, not geography. A geo-looking cookie is NOT a geo-block signal.

markers.s: Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker

botwall.dist: Third DataDome instance, 1707 bytes, 50 visible-text chars. Confirms the DataDome body template is host-independent, so vendor detection generalizes while host heuristics do not.
botwall.notes: Also carries a Cloudflare __cf_bm cookie in the same response: two bot vendors stacked on one request. Do not assume one wall per response.

botwall.dist: THE STATUS-CODE TRAP: HTTP 202 Accepted. Any classifier that treats 2xx as success and only inspects 4xx/5xx for walls will pass this straight through as a real page.
botwall.notes: AWS WAF challenge served via CloudFront. x-amzn-waf-action: challenge is also listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers, so it is visible to browser JS. Fourth distinct bot vendor in this corpus.

maintenance.dist: SYNTHETIC. Carries the 503 status and NOTHING else - zero-byte body, no Retry-After, no maintenance copy. Distinguishing maintenance from rate_limited or a transient 5xx is impossible from this sample alone.
maintenance.notes: Body is 0 bytes. Included only to pin the status-code branch of the classifier. Real maintenance pages usually add a Retry-After header and human copy; neither is present here.

No live maintenance window occurred across the ~37 pages fetched. Planned maintenance is short, unannounced to third parties, and cannot be induced without attacking a host. Collect opportunistically: watch production traffic for 503 responses whose body contains maintenance or back-soon copy, and archive them when they appear.

rate_limited.dist: SYNTHETIC. Status only; body is 0 bytes and there is NO Retry-After header, which is exactly what a real rate-limit response would carry.
rate_limited.notes: Documents the shape but not the evidence. A production 429 fixture should be kept for the Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers, which are the actual discriminators.

DELIBERATELY NOT COLLECTED. Inducing a real 429 means hammering a third-party server, which the collection rules forbid. Harvest these from your own production traffic instead, where they occur naturally, and keep the full header block.

http_404.dist: vs login_required: GitHub returns 404 for private repos you cannot see, so an identical 404 can mean absent or exists-but-forbidden. Unresolvable from the response.
http_404.notes: Real HTTP 404 with a large branded error page (267KB decompressed). Page size is not a 404 signal.

markers.s: Leider gibt es die von Ihnen gesuchte Seite nicht oder nicht mehr.

http_404.dist: Textbook 404: correct status AND explicit copy, in German. Note that no English not-found string appears anywhere, so English-only keyword lists fail on this file.
http_404.notes: Smallest real 404 collected (18KB, 268 visible-text chars). Also notable: this host serves a consent wall on its homepage but NOT on its 404 page.

http_404.dist: Correct 404 status but served with the site's FULL navigation (268KB decompressed), larger than several successful pages in this corpus. Confirms body size is orthogonal to error state.
http_404.notes: Contrast with paywall_saas/statista_statistic.html from the same host: same chrome, different status and different gating markup.

http_404.dist: A 404 page that ALSO carries the site's age-gate markup. One document, two categories. Any single-label classifier is wrong on this file no matter which label it picks.
http_404.notes: 144KB. Strong argument for multi-label output over single-label classification.

http_404.dist: WRONG-STATUS CASE: a missing page answered with HTTP 400 Bad Request, not 404, and the copy says something-went-wrong rather than not-found. Neither the status nor the text says missing.
http_404.notes: Closest thing to a soft-404 collected. Shows that status-to-category mapping needs a 4xx bucket, not a 404 equality test.

http_404.dist: NEGATIVE CONTROL and the hardest file here: HTTP 200 after a 307/302/302/302 chain across two domains, 20KB of HTML, and SIX visible-text characters. It is not a 404, not a login page, and not a wall; it is an empty client-rendered shell.
http_404.notes: Any almost-no-text-means-blocked rule fires here and is wrong. Without executing JavaScript the true state is genuinely unknowable.

http_500.dist: SYNTHETIC, zero-byte body. Only the status line carries information.
http_500.notes: Pairs with mockhttpstatus_500 to show that 500 bodies range from nothing at all to a one-line string.

http_500.dist: SYNTHETIC. 25-byte body containing only the status text, no HTML tags at all, so an HTML parser yields nothing to match on.
http_500.notes: Smallest fixture in the corpus. Useful for testing that the classifier does not crash on non-HTML bodies.

No genuine 5xx occurred across ~37 fetches to 25 hosts, which is itself a finding: real server errors are rare enough on major sites that they cannot be scheduled. Collect opportunistically from production traffic.

gdpr_consent.dist: STRONGEST consent signal in the corpus: __tcfapi appears 7 times and the Sourcepoint CMP is loaded by name 17 times. The IAB TCF v2 API surface is what separates a consent wall from any other interstitial.
gdpr_consent.notes: Served in full to a Korean (non-EU) IP, so the CMP fires unconditionally rather than by geography. HTTP 200, 1.39MB decompressed.

gdpr_consent.dist: vs zeit_home: same category, far weaker evidence. __tcfapi appears only twice and no CMP vendor is named in the served HTML. A threshold tuned on zeit_home may not fire here.
gdpr_consent.notes: 3.98MB (decompressed) homepage that ALSO advertises the SPIEGEL+ subscription product, so consent and paywall markers coexist without this page itself being paywalled.

gdpr_consent.dist: DUAL-CATEGORY: the same document is the paywall_news sample. __tcfapi marks the consent layer, edi_medium=paywall marks the subscription layer, and both are true simultaneously.
gdpr_consent.notes: Identical file to paywall_news/lemonde_article.html (one fetch, copied). The canonical argument for multi-label classification.
